12:     - All /tasks/* endpoints require "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

14:       tasks. A task belonging to another user (or no task at all) returns
15:       404, so existence of other users' tasks is never leaked.

48: 
49:     This is safe to run against a pre-existing database created before the
50:     ``users`` table / ``tasks.owner_id`` column existed: it only adds what's
51:     missing and never drops or rewrites existing rows.
52:     """
53:     conn = sqlite3.connect(database_path)
54:     try:
55:         conn.execute(
56:             "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users ("
57:             "  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,"
58:             "  username TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,"
59:             "  password_hash TEXT NOT NULL"
60:             ")"
61:         )

172: def generate_token(secret: str, user_id: int, username: str) -> str:
173:     payload = {
174:         "user_id": user_id,
175:         "username": username,
176:         "exp": datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(seconds=TOKEN_EXPIRY_SECONDS),
177:     }
178:     token = jwt.encode(payload, secret, algorithm=JWT_ALGORITHM)
179:     # PyJWT >= 2 returns a str already; guard against older versions returning bytes.
180:     return token.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(token, bytes) else token

182: 
183: def decode_token(secret: str, token: str) -> dict:
184:     return jwt.decode(token, secret, algorithms=[JWT_ALGORITHM])

187: def login_required(view):
188:     """Require a valid ``Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`` header.
189: 
190:     On success, sets ``g.current_user`` (dict with ``id``/``username``) and
191:     calls the wrapped view. Otherwise returns a 401 JSON error.
192:     """
193: 
194:     @wraps(view)
195:     def wrapped(*args, **kwargs):
196:         auth_header = request.headers.get("Authorization", "")
197:         if not auth_header.startswith("Bearer "):
198:             return jsonify({"error": "missing or invalid authorization header"}), 401
199: 
200:         token = auth_header[len("Bearer "):].strip()
201:         if not token:
202:             return jsonify({"error": "missing or invalid authorization header"}), 401
203: 
204:         try:
205:             payload = decode_token(current_app.config["JWT_SECRET"], token)

207:             return jsonify({"error": "token has expired"}), 401
208:         except jwt.InvalidTokenError:
209:             return jsonify({"error": "invalid token"}), 401
210: 
211:         user = get_user_by_id(payload.get("user_id"))
212:         if user is None:
213:             return jsonify({"error": "invalid token"}), 401
214: 
215:         g.current_user = user
216:         return view(*args, **kwargs)

218:     return wrapped

def register(client, username="alice", password="s3cret-pw"):
    return client.post(
        "/auth/register",
        data=json.dumps({"username": username, "password": password}),
        content_type="application/json",
    )


def login(client, username="alice", password="s3cret-pw"):
    return client.post(
        "/auth/login",
        data=json.dumps({"username": username, "password": password}),
        content_type="application/json",
    )


def auth_headers(token):
    return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}


@pytest.fixture
def token(client):
    """Register + login a default user, returning a valid JWT."""
    register(client, "alice", "s3cret-pw")
    resp = login(client, "alice", "s3cret-pw")
    return resp.get_json()["token"]


def create(client, token, title="Buy milk"):
    return client.post(
        "/tasks",
        data=json.dumps({"title": title}),
        content_type="application/json",
        headers=auth_headers(token),
    )


# ── POST /auth/register ─────────────────────────────────────

def test_register_success(client):
    resp = register(client, "bob", "password123")
    assert resp.status_code == 201
    body = resp.get_json()
    assert body["username"] == "bob"
    assert isinstance(body["id"], int)
    assert "password" not in body
    assert "password_hash" not in body

    register(client, "bob", "password123")

    with app.app_context():

        row = get_db().execute(

    assert row["password_hash"] != "password123"

Celery tasks for the Task Management API.

Currently just one task: sending a (mocked) notification email to a task's
owner when their task is marked completed. The task is intentionally
side-effect-light (a log/print) so it can run in any environment without
real SMTP credentials; swap the body for a real email provider call when
ready.
"""

import logging

from celery_app import celery_app

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@celery_app.task(name="tasks.send_notification_email")
def send_notification_email(user_email: str, task_title: str) -> str:
    """Send (mock) a "task completed" notification email.

    Runs asynchronously on a Celery worker so the HTTP request that
    triggered it never blocks waiting on this. For now, "sending" just
    means logging/printing -- swap in a real email provider integration
    (SendGrid, SES, SMTP, etc.) here when one is available.
    """
    message = (
        f"[email notification] To: {user_email} | "
        f"Subject: Task completed | "
        f"Body: Your task '{task_title}' has been marked as completed."
    )
    print(message)
    logger.info(message)
    return message
